content.executive_summary:
- **Sole ITED Acting Head**: Prof. Dr. Ursel Fantz (Garching, Ursel.Fantz@ipp.mpg.de, +49 89 3299-1958) oversees three groups (Neutral Beam Injection, ITER Diagnostic, Plasma for Gas Conversion); she is the single correct entry point for ITER technology hires -> Initiate contact by emailing her with a one-page CV + ITER-specific instrumentation thesis summary.
- **ITER Diagnostic Group Bolometry/Pressure Gauntlet**: Dr. Hans Meister (Garching, hans.meister@ipp.mpg.de, +49 89 3299-1885, +49 89 3299-2558) heads bolometer and ionisation-pressure-gauge electronics for the ITER Upper Ports -> he is the highest-fit PI for Harsh Desai's FPGA/DAQ background.
- **W7-X Scientific Director at Greifswald**: Prof. Dr. Thomas Klinger (thomas.klinger@ipp.mpg.de, +49 3834 88 2501) leads the Stellarator Dynamics and Transport division; his group runs W7-X's instrumentation-heavy campaigns.
- **Greifswald NBI / Heating Power Base**: Prof. Dr. Robert Wolf (Director since 2006, PhD at JET, phone +49 38 3488-1205) is the senior experimental-heating/NBI contact; PhD at JET places his work at the centre of ITER-relevant neutral beam physics.
- **ASDEX Upgrade Directors Driving Scenario Work**: Dr. Rachael McDermott (Director since 2023) and Dr. Tim Happel (Director, leaving IPP for a TUM chair in 2026) build the ITER-physics-base scenarios AUG runs; both lead PhD cohorts that route through the IPP doctoral framework.
- **IPP Has No "IMPRS-IPP"**: Doctorate is via direct IPP group application + a co-registered PhD at Technical University of Munich (Garching) or University of Greifswald, plus the EUROfusion Engineering Grant and the IHGS graduate school at Forschungszentrum Julich -> apply concurrently, not sequentially.
- **Career Portals Triad**: Application URLs are split between `ipp.mpg.de` open positions, the Max Planck Society `mpg.de` job board, and EUROfusion's `euro-fusion.org` research-grant portal; EURAXESS lists Germany postings including IPP under researcher mobility.
- **Best Two-Track Application for Desai**: E-mail Meister + Fantz for instrumentation-track PhDs while submitting a EUROfusion Engineering Grant (deadlines late winter) and an EURAXESS Germany posting; the IMPRS-IPP brand does not exist as a separate school.
- **Demo Stellarator 'Alpha' Greenlit 26 Feb 2026**: IPP's Garching site will host a demonstration stellarator 'Alpha' (announced 26 Feb 2026) -> creates a forward hiring signal beyond ITER.

ITER-relevant work concentrates in three places: the ITER Technology & Diagnostics (ITED) division at Garching; ASDEX Upgrade operations at Garching; and W7-X experimental campaigns at Greifswald IPP LinkedIn.

content.iter_diagnostics_group_bolometer_and_pre:
The ITER Diagnostic Group under Meister develops ITER upper-port bolometers and ionisation pressure gauges; both designs trace back to IPP patents from the 1980s for ASDEX and ASDEX Upgrade [iter_diagnostics_group_bolometer_and_pressure_gauge_pipelines[0]] [12]. Bolometer instrumentation is the single highest-fit area for FPGA-based detector readout because the IPP bolometer-camera electronics are upgraded every experimental campaign and depend heavily on DAQ throughput, fast ADC sampling, and high-voltage biasing of the bolometer bridge resistors.

Implication: a candidate with vacuum/DAQ/high-voltage test expertise aligns directly with how IPP bolometer cameras are characterised and certified. Recommendation: in the cover email, reference ITER upper port design codes, bolometer-grade amplifier design, and the IPP bolometer group's published noise spectra to short-circuit the screening filter.
content.greifswald_nbi_and_heating_architecture:
Robert Wolf's directorship (since 2006) and his JET PhD make him IPP's senior figure for ITER-relevant heating and current drive [greifswald_nbi_and_heating_architecture[0]] [52]. The NBI sub-group under ITED, hosted jointly with Fantz's division, again leverages IPP's ELISE and BATMAN test stands (negative ion sources) and feeds directly into ITER's neutral beam heating line via the ITER Neutral Beam Test Facility contributions.

Implication: instrumentation work for NBI test stands (high-voltage isolation of the ion source, calorimeter DAQ, beam diagnostics) is a structured workstream at IPP, and Wolf is the senior refereeing voice for any PhD touching negative-ion beam technology. Recommendation: if the candidate's vacuum/HV background is the primary hook, lead with Wolf; if FPGA/SIMION particle-tracking is the hook, route through Firmenzent instead.
content.w7_x_greifswald_diagnostics_operations_a:
Thomas Klinger directs W7-X operations since 2005 and leads the W7-X Instrumentation Division [w7_x_greifswald_diagnostics_operations_and_engineering_technology[0]] [42]. W7-X's diagnostic suite includes Thomson scattering, X-ray imaging, bolometry, and spectroscopy tools built and maintained by IPP's diagnostic engineering group. Head of W7-X Engineering Technology (LinkedIn, public) is Axel Lorenz, a co-located contact for instrument-engineering roles Axel Lorenz LinkedIn.

Implication: W7-X is the primary German stellarator and a recurring source of ITER-relevant diagnostic methodology (long-pulse data acquisition, water-cooled detector heads). Recommendation: for high-voltage/fast-DAQ PhDs on stellarators, name W7-X and Klinger explicitly and request a co-supervised PhD with the University of Greifswald.
content.asdex_upgrade_iter_plasma_scenario_test_:
McDermott took over as IPP Director focused on ASDEX Upgrade plasma scenarios in 2023 [asdex_upgrade_iter_plasma_scenario_test_bed[0]] [58]; Happel leads ASDEX-related diagnostics until his 2026 transition to a TUM professorship [asdex_upgrade_iter_plasma_scenario_test_bed[1]] [8]. AUG runs the ITER-shape tungsten divertor and is in the middle of an upgrade with new divertor coils [asdex_upgrade_iter_plasma_scenario_test_bed[2]] [65].

Implication: AUG divertor-coil commissioning (2026) drives a near-term need for diagnostic DAQ refits and high-voltage instrumentation testing. Recommendation: candidates with HV bias experience and space-plasma instrument heritage should pitch directly to AUG divertor instrumentation teams; Happel's transition opens a successor position for a PhD cohort lead.
content.application_routes_and_career_portals:
IPP routes PhD applicants through three parallel channels:

- **Direct IPP application route** (group-by-group): identify a PI from this map and email the PI directly with a CV + project proposal; supervisors co-register you at TU Munich (Garching) or Ernst-Moritz-Arndt University Greifswald. The IPP pages do not advertise a dedicated "IMPRS-IPP"; the IMPRS-PHDS mentioned in IMPRS pages is unrelated (it trains demographers and epidemiologists).
- **Max Planck Society career route**: the MPG hosts all IPP director-level positions on https://www.mpg.de and routes senior scientist roles there; for staff positions, route through https://www.ipp.mpg.de directly per `ipp.mpg.de/jobs`-style pages (search engine indexed forms at https://www.ipp.mpg.de/17167/userspace for IPP internal-only resources).
- **EUROfusion / EURAXESS route**: EUROfusion's research-grant portal lists Engineering Grants and PostDoc Grants routed through IPP's Garching and Greifswald sites EUROfusion Project; EURAXESS lists Germany research positions including IPP under EURAXESS Jobs.

Recommendation: send one cover email to Meister + one to Wolf within 10 days of opening a position; in parallel, list yourself on the EUROfusion engineering-grant portal because the dataset in the EURAXESS portal refreshes every quarter with new IPP openings.
content.harsh_desai_fit_ranking:
| Rank | PI / Lead | Group | Fit Dimension | Fit Score (1-5) | Risk / Caveat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dr. Hans Meister (ITER Diagnostics, Garching) | Bolometers + ITER pressure gauges | High-voltage detector readout, FPGA DAQ, vacuum HV tests | 5 | ITER-only; may require ITER security clearance |
| 2 | Prof. Dr. Ursel Fantz (ITED Acting Head) | All of ITED including NBI | Cross-group access, can route to NBI or Diagnostics | 5 | Acting head; portfolio time constrained |
| 3 | Prof. Dr. Robert Wolf (NBI/heating) | Negative-ion NBI test stands | SIMION beam optics, HV, vacuum beam diagnostics | 4 | ITER NBI test stand role not yet funded for 2026 |
| 4 | Prof. Dr. Thomas Klinger (W7-X director) | Stellarator Dynamics & Transport | Long-pulse DAQ, control software, instrumentation | 4 | Stellarator focus, lower direct ITER lineage |
| 5 | Dr. Rachael McDermott (ASDEX Upgrade Director) | AUG plasma scenarios | AUG-specific diagnostic instrumentation, HV, FPGA | 4 | Cohort scheduling may rotate around Happel/TUM transition |
| 6 | Dr. Tim Happel (ASDEX Director, transition 2026) | AUG scenarios and divertor upgrade | Divertor diagnostic DAQ refit | 3 | Transitioning to TUM 2026; cohort handover risk |
| 7 | Prof. Dr. Per Helander (Theory) | Stellarator Theory | SRIM/SIMION space-plasma skills applicable | 2 | Pure theory group, not instrumentation-fit |

Top fit is Meister because his group's deliverable is the ITER upper-port bolometer camera -- and bolometers are precisely where FPGA detector readout, DAQ pipeline, and HV bias experience converge. Wolf's NBI work folds in SRIM-relevant beam optics and SIMION modelling. Klinger is the right W7-X surface; McDermott and Happel, despite Happel's transition, are surfaceable for ASDEX Upgrade diagnostic instrumentation work. Helander is the wrong top-level candidate for an instrumentation PhD, although his theory group's tools benefit from SRIM/SIMION exposure.

Takeaways: the candidate's M.Eng Space Systems UMich background is convertible at IPP via bolometer/HV/DAQ work (Meister), and via beam test stands (Wolf). Failing both routes, fall back on the AUG divertor upgrade lead via McDermott.
content.synthesis_routing_strategy_and_time_boun: IPP's ITER-relevant portfolio is structurally narrow: ITED (Fantz + 3 sub-groups) at Garching; W7-X (Klinger, Wolf, Helander) at Greifswald; AUG (McDermott, Happel) at Garching. Of these, only Fantz, Meister, and Klinger carry public phone numbers, and only Meister and Wolf run instrumentation-heavy PhD pipelines. Harsh Desai's strongest alignment is Meister (ITER bolometer cameras), with Wolf as parallel route, Klinger as W7-X fallback, and McDermott/Happel as AUG divertor-instrumentation fallback. The application is not via one "IMPRS-IPP" school but through three concurrent tracks: direct IPP group application, EUROfusion engineering-grant portal, and EURAXESS Germany listings; the IMPRS-IPP brand does not appear in IPP's English website. The forward signals (Alpha demonstration stellarator in Garching, AUG divertor-coil commissioning, ongoing W7-X experimental campaigns) create inventory for the 2026-2027 hiring window.
